considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(sale, at), 5), NEG(RATIO(che, lct))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with volatile revenue productivity and weak cash coverage of current liabilities are genuinely fragile and should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the gross-margin/cost-structure channel with demand uncertainty and cash-runway risk. R&D assets are hard to pledge and often require continuing funding, so unstable sales combined with low liquidity makes apparent distress more likely to become binding financial distress.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Noncash-Earnings Quality Gap
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(gdwl, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(pi, oancf), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill-heavy firms whose pretax income is not backed by operating cash flow are more likely to face acquisition-quality problems and future impairment risk.
considered.reasoning: This moves away from another goodwill-liquidity or goodwill-leverage template and focuses on earnings quality after acquisitions. A large positive gap between accounting income and cash flow is especially concerning when goodwill is high, because reported profitability may not provide real resources to absorb impairment or financing shocks.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Renewal Cash-Cover
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(intan, at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms expanding capitalized intangibles while generating operating cash flow against liabilities should outperform because intangible renewal is financeable rather than distressed.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the criticized intangibles-level-times-leverage trap and does not treat routine amortization as impairment. Growth in capitalized intangibles is interpreted positively only when operating cash flow provides liability coverage, separating productive intangible renewal from stranded-asset fragility.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Cash-Flow Trough Recovery
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)), RATIO(che, lct)))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms recovering from prior operating-cash-flow troughs while holding adequate liquidity should outperform as apparent distress recedes.
considered.reasoning: The signal targets a recovery state rather than a static cash-flow level: current operating cash generation has improved relative to the firm’s own downside history. Cash-to-current-liabilities coverage helps ensure that the rebound is financially usable and not merely an accounting or cyclical bounce without runway.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Tax-Validated Goodwill Solvency
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(gdwl, at)), RANK(RATIO(txt, lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill-heavy firms that generate taxable profits relative to liabilities should outperform because their acquired intangible assets are more likely productive than impaired.
considered.reasoning: Goodwill is not always a distress signal; it is problematic when acquisition accounting is unsupported by real earnings capacity. Tax expense relative to liabilities provides an external profitability validation channel that can separate successful acquisitions from fragile goodwill-heavy balance sheets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Adjusted Net-Income Recovery
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(ni, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with improving R&D-adjusted net income should outperform because their apparent accounting distress is being resolved by productive knowledge investment.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the 5-year floor template with a recovery mechanism based on change in adjusted profitability. Adding back R&D addresses accounting expensing, while improvement in adjusted net income indicates that the firm is moving away from genuine operating fragility rather than merely showing a stable historical minimum.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Working-Capital Integration Strain
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms adding goodwill while working capital deteriorates are more likely experiencing acquisition-integration strain and should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This moves away from the static goodwill-load, thin-equity, cash-burn construction and instead tests a dynamic post-acquisition balance-sheet strain. Rising goodwill can be benign, but if working capital weakens at the same time, the acquisition may be consuming liquidity or failing to convert into operating resilience.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Purchased-Intangible Renewal Deficit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(re, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with large identifiable acquired intangibles, little internal R&D renewal, and deteriorating retained earnings should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the prior turnover-stress template and does not divide sales by small intangible balances. The mechanism is that acquired intangible assets become stranded when the firm is not replenishing knowledge internally and accumulated profitability is worsening.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with cash-heavy current assets should outperform because their liquidity is more immediately usable to sustain knowledge investment.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the working-capital-volatility mirror with a current-asset quality mechanism. For intangible-intensive firms, cash as a larger share of current assets helps distinguish real funding runway from liquidity that depends on less liquid working-capital components.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Runway Erosion
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), RANK(NEG(TREND(WINSOR(RATIO(che, ADD(dlc, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 1), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with deteriorating cash runway relative to short debt and ongoing R&D spending are genuinely fragile and should underperform.
considered.reasoning: The level of cash runway can look adequate temporarily, but a persistent downward trend indicates the firm is consuming liquidity faster than it can replenish it. For R&D-heavy firms, that erosion raises the risk of forced cuts to knowledge investment, refinancing pressure, or shareholder dilution.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Taxable Book-Distress Wedge
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(txt, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ib, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with low book income but meaningful tax expense should outperform because traditional accounting distress is overstated.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the scale-collapsing MIN construction and does not reuse gross-surplus or cash-flow-floor legs. The signal requires a book-distress symptom and tax validation at the same time, isolating firms whose expensed knowledge investment may depress reported earnings despite real taxable profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D External Equity Funding Strain
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), RANK(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(ceq, at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(re, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms whose book equity is improving more through external capital than retained earnings are likely funding knowledge investment from financial strain and should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the simple maturity-plus-liquidity blend with an external-financing dependence mechanism. If equity capital rises without retained-earnings repair, the firm may be diluting shareholders to sustain R&D rather than demonstrating internally financed knowledge productivity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Ranked R&D Tax-Cash Coverage
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(txt, lt)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with both tax-validated profitability and operating cash-flow coverage of liabilities should outperform.
considered.reasoning: Ranking the tax and cash channels before multiplying avoids the original MIN scale problem where the smaller tax ratio dominated the signal. The interaction requires dual confirmation that the intangible-heavy firm can support liabilities through both taxable earnings and operating cash generation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Tax-Validation Deterioration
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(txt, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms adding goodwill while tax-validated profitability deteriorates are more likely experiencing poor acquisition quality and should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the accruals-minus-tax construction and no longer overlaps mechanically with the noncash-earnings-quality gap. Goodwill accretion is most concerning when the acquired asset base is followed by declining tax profitability, suggesting weaker real earnings capacity and greater impairment risk.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Acquired-Intangible Cash-Conversion Strain
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), SUMRANK(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)), 1), RATIO(lct, at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with large identifiable acquired intangibles should underperform when sales growth is not converting into operating cash flow and current liabilities are elevated.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the unstable sale-to-intangibles denominator and is not just the sign-flipped renewal-deficit formula. The mechanism is cash-conversion strain: acquired intangibles may be generating accounting or revenue growth, but if cash flow fails to follow while near-term obligations are high, the intangible base is more likely financially fragile.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Gross-Profit Cash-Quality Floor
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(che, act))))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with durable gross-profit capacity and cash-heavy current assets are more likely to be accounting-distressed than genuinely fragile.
considered.reasoning: The multi-year gross-profit floor asks whether the firm has maintained an economic surplus before expensed knowledge investment. Cash as a share of current assets provides a liquidity-quality filter, favoring firms whose current assets can actually support continued R&D through stress.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Revenue-Obligation Scale
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(sale, lct)))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with revenue scale large relative to current liabilities should outperform because commercialization capacity reduces the likelihood that accounting distress becomes binding financial distress.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the criticized cash-runway construction with a top-line commercialization-versus-obligation mechanism. The signal asks whether the firm has enough operating scale to support near-term claims while continuing knowledge investment, rather than reusing cash plus short-debt coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Taxable Turnaround Liquidity
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(txt, at), 1), RATIO(act, lct)))
considered.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with improving tax-validated profitability and adequate current liquidity should outperform as accounting distress concerns fade.
considered.reasoning: This avoids another adjusted-net-income operator swap and instead uses tax-expense improvement as an external validation of economic recovery. Pairing the tax turnaround with current liquidity helps separate firms whose R&D is becoming self-sustaining from firms whose apparent recovery lacks financial runway.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Retained-Equity Quality
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(re, ADD(ABS(re), ABS(ceq)))))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms whose equity base is supported by retained earnings rather than external equity dependence should outperform.
considered.reasoning: This addresses the ambiguity in changes in book equity by focusing on the composition and quality of the equity cushion. For intangible-heavy firms, retained earnings support indicates that prior R&D has generated cumulative profitability, reducing the chance that solvency improvement is merely issuance-funded.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Cash-Quality Erosion
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(gdwl, at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(che, act), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill-heavy firms whose current assets are becoming less cash-rich are more likely to face acquisition-integration strain and should underperform.
considered.reasoning: This avoids combining cash burn with a tax leg that prior evidence made ambiguous. The mechanism is deterioration in liquidity quality: goodwill is more fragile when the firm’s current-asset base is shifting away from immediately usable cash, raising impairment and refinancing risk.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Acquired-Intangible Demand Instability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(sale, at), 5), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms with large identifiable acquired intangibles should underperform when demand productivity is volatile and gross margins are deteriorating.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the renewal-deficit plus liquidity-gap recombination with an operating-instability mechanism. Acquired intangibles are more likely to become stranded when sales productivity is unstable and margins weaken, indicating that the acquired asset base is not producing durable economic returns.

critic_notes.rationale: The R&D-addback-to-liabilities conditioning on R&D intensity is internally consistent and the positive sign follows naturally from the expression, but the construct is close to a mechanical blend of two documented effects (R&D intensity premium and profitability/debt-coverage) and xrd/sale is unstable for low-sales firms, so incremental novelty is modest.

The loss indicator zeroes out the majority of firms, so the resulting spread mechanically goes long loss-making R&D firms and short *all* profitable firms — a bet against the profitability premium that the stated hypothesis never claims, on top of a severely degenerate mass-at-zero distribution.

The hypothesis, expression and negative sign line up cleanly and the R&D-acceleration × net-short-debt interaction is not a direct rediscovery, though the second leg is largely a repackaged cash/short-term-leverage distress measure and ACCEL of a ratio is noisy at annual frequency.

Economically coherent and correctly signed, but it is close to a straightforward "bad balance sheet is bad" composite of two familiar ingredients (goodwill intensity and working-capital deficiency) with limited genuinely cross-theme insight.

The negative-book-equity indicator restricts the informative long leg to a few percent of firms while assigning zero to everything else, guaranteeing sparse, unstable portfolio composition — exactly the coverage-driven artifact the objective warns against.

Signs and logic are consistent, but adding a flow (xrd) to a stock (intan) is dimensionally sloppy and the cash-burn-plus-leverage leg largely reproduces standard distress-risk underperformance, making this the most generic of the batch.

This is a cosmetic re-specification of the archived "R&D Cash-Earnings Resilience" signal (identical second leg, R&D denominator swapped from sale to at, RANK→IND_RANK), and its second leg is essentially the negative-accruals (Sloan) anomaly, so it offers little new economic content.

Near-duplicate of the archived "Knowledge-Adjusted Equity Runway" — the same cumulative-R&D-addback-over-liabilities construction with re substituted for ceq and the current-ratio leg dropped — which is a mechanical variant rather than a diagnosis of that signal's flat Fama-MacBeth slope.

The second leg is identical to the archived "R&D Debt-Wall Acceleration" and the first leg merely swaps ACCEL for a 3-year MA and sale for at, so this is a smoothing tweak of an already-tested signal rather than a substantively different mechanism.

COALESCE(xad,0) conflates non-reporting firms with genuine zero advertisers, so the first RANK collapses to a large tied mass and the signal will largely degenerate into the second leg — which itself recycles the already-tested accruals/liquidity composite.

Internally inconsistent construction: Compustat intan includes gdwl, so MAX(intan/at, gdwl/at) reduces to intan/at and the "acquired-goodwill" distinction is not actually captured, while the second leg (leverage + negative retained earnings) is a textbook Altman/Ohlson distress composite already probed by the archived goodwill signal.

Substituting cash-flow volatility for the archived signal's cash-burn level introduces a genuinely different mechanism — unpledgeable knowledge assets financed with debt under uncertain internal funding — with a coherent negative sign, though coverage will thin from the 5-year volatility window and cash-flow volatility alone is a partially documented predictor.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover" (identical first leg, and a liability-coverage second leg that merely swaps gross surplus for pre-R&D cash flow), and it also overlaps heavily with "R&D Cash-Earnings Resilience," so it tests the same coverage-of-liabilities construct already established.

The legs (margin *change* plus cash-to-current-liabilities runway) are meaningfully different from the archived level-based coverage and sales-growth/leverage variants, though it remains in the crowded "R&D intensity × good news" family and margin improvement is close to the known change-in-gross-profitability effect.

The hypothesis is a conditional-attenuation claim ("negative working capital is *less* distressing"), but the expression is monotonically increasing in negative working capital and therefore asserts an outright positive premium for working-capital deficits — contradicting the archived Goodwill/Retrenchment liquidity-squeeze results — and the triple rank product concentrates the portfolio in a thin corner while embedding the known gross-profitability anomaly as the likely driver.

This is the archived "Goodwill Liquidity Squeeze" with one extra leg bolted on, and that added leg is problematic since low/negative sales growth is a classic value-side characteristic historically associated with *higher* subsequent returns, working against the stated negative expected sign.

The internal-versus-acquired intangible composition leg is a genuinely new construct relative to the archive, but note that subtracting raw ratios before ranking lets the larger-magnitude gdwl/at dominate (making it mostly a low-goodwill screen), and the solvency leg repeats the liability-coverage motif already tested.

The dynamic framing (rising liabilities alongside deteriorating gross surplus, conditional on R&D intensity) is a defensible and sign-consistent departure from the archive's static leverage screens, though both legs individually echo well-known debt-issuance and profitability-change anomalies so incremental novelty comes only from the interaction.

This is a cosmetic rescaling of the archive's best performer ("R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover", fmb 4.15/talpha 3.52) — swapping the denominator from total liabilities to current liabilities plus a small xrd term leaves the same economic construct and highly correlated rank ordering, so it tests denominator sensitivity rather than a new mechanism.

The expression is internally consistent with the stated negative sign and the R&D-addback loss *level* is a substantively different second leg from the archive's gross-margin-deterioration spiral, though it recombines two already-tested channels (addback profitability, liability growth) and inherits the earlier spiral's risk of a strong FMB slope with negligible portfolio alpha.

This is a direct rediscovery of the archived "Internal-Knowledge Solvency Mix" with the only change being SUB of two raw ratios replaced by SUMRANK of the same two ratios — a pure normalization tweak, not a new hypothesis.

The goodwill-share-of-equity-cushion construct is a genuinely different framing from the archive's gdwl/at scalings and pairs coherently with cash burn, but the ratio gdwl/(gdwl+ceq) is non-monotonic and sign-flipping when ceq is negative — exactly the distressed population targeted — so winsorization alone will not prevent the most fragile firms from landing in the wrong tail.

This is a mechanical transplant that bolts the first leg of "Liquidity-Forced R&D Retrenchment" (retrenchment in intangible spending) onto the *identical* second leg of "Advertising Liquidity Squeeze" ((lct−che)/at), at ~4–5% coverage, so it is a recombination of tested parts rather than a new mechanism.

It is close to the sign-mirror of the already-tested "R&D Liquidity Repair Reinvestment" (which failed on the portfolio leg), the interaction_type field is blank, and the core interaction is partly mechanical since higher cash R&D spending directly reduces working capital — so a hit would be hard to distinguish from an accounting identity.

Internally consistent and the burn-rate denominator (dlc + R&D spend) is a defensible twist on the runway idea, but it sits close to the already-tested che/lct and cash-to-liability coverage legs in the archive, so expect substantial overlap rather than fresh information.

This is essentially the sign-flipped "Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor" (TS_MIN → NEG TS_RANK of oancf/at) bolted onto the debt leg from the already-failed "R&D Cash-Flow Volatility Debt Trap," making it a cosmetic recombination of two archived signals rather than a new mechanism.

Substituting second-moment stability for the archived level-based "R&D Working-Capital Normalization" is a genuine change in signal content, though the low-fundamental-volatility leg risks proxying the known earnings/cash-flow volatility anomaly and size, so any alpha should be checked against those controls.

This is the archived "Goodwill Equity-Cushion Cash Burn" with ceq replaced by ABS(ceq) — a one-function robustness tweak affecting only the small negative-equity tail, not a substantively different signal.

The impairment-plus-refinancing story is coherent and the margin-erosion leg is a real departure from the archive's liquidity/net-debt goodwill conditioners, though it remains a mashup of previously used components and the leverage leg will largely reproduce the earlier goodwill-leverage results.

Cash taxes are a genuinely different, harder-to-manipulate validation channel than the archive's gross-surplus, accrual, and cash-flow addback legs, but txt/lt is close enough to a scaled profitability ratio that FF5's RMW may absorb much of the alpha, so the marginal contribution over "R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover" is the key thing to measure.

The first leg divides by gross profit, so firms with negative or near-zero gross surplus (the most fragile ones) receive large-magnitude negative ratios and land in the low-rank "safe" bucket, inverting the intended ordering and contradicting the stated hypothesis; the second leg (lct/act) is also a mechanical re-scaling of the already-tested lct−act liquidity squeeze legs.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "R&D-Adjusted Loss Liability Spiral" — identical R&D leg and identical NEG((pi+xrd)/at) addback term with only the second distress component swapped from liability growth to cash-balance change — so it tests essentially the same mechanism already documented.

Debt maturity structure ((dltt−dlc)/lt) is a genuinely new second leg relative to the archive's level-based leverage and net-debt legs, the duration-matching rationale for long-lived R&D assets is economically coherent, and the expression's direction cleanly matches the positive expected sign.

It is effectively the sign-flipped recombination of two archived signals ("Intangible Sales-Efficiency Runway" and "Intangible Cash-Burn Leverage Trap"), and the sale/intan term is numerically unstable for firms with tiny intangible balances, so the sort will be driven by scaling outliers rather than the stranded-asset mechanism.

This is a near-mechanical substitution into the archived "Goodwill Margin-Erosion Debt Overhang" (same gdwl/at × SUMRANK(distress, lt/at) template) with a low-tax leg borrowed from other archived signals, and low txt/at is largely a proxy for low profitability, making the composite close to a trivial goodwill-times-low-profitability-times-leverage screen.

The contrarian pairing of tax-validated current profitability with a *level* accumulated-deficit (rather than the archived delta-RE version) is internally consistent and economically motivated, though it sits uncomfortably close to the already-tested "Tax-Paying R&D Solvency" and "R&D No-Tax Deficit Drift" and risks being dominated by the well-known negative RE/at distress effect.

This is essentially a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "R&D Debt-Wall Acceleration" (ACCEL→DELTA of R&D intensity, (dlc−che)/at→dlc/lt) and overlaps the maturity-tilt leg of "R&D Maturity-Matched Financing," so it adds no new mechanism.

The expression is close to the sign-flipped union of two archived signals ("R&D Liability-Growth Spiral" and "R&D Accumulated-Deficit Repair"/"R&D No-Tax Deficit Drift"), making it a recombination rather than a new mechanism.

GROWTH(cogs/sale) is mechanically the negative of gross-margin growth, so this reproduces the archived R&D × margin-erosion × current-liability structure ("R&D Margin-Trough Current Burden," "R&D Liability-Growth Spiral") with a swapped margin proxy.

The cash-versus-current-liability leg duplicates "Goodwill Liquidity Squeeze"/"Goodwill Net-Debt Collateral Gap," and the only increment (dlc/lt maturity share) is too thin to constitute a distinct hypothesis in a family already showing consistently negative but fmb-insignificant results.

Conditioning goodwill accretion on subsequent operating cash-flow and margin deterioration is a substantively different second leg from the financing-side "Debt-Financed Goodwill Accretion" (whose fmb/alpha signs disagreed), and the expression's direction matches the stated negative sign, though it remains adjacent to the well-documented acquirer-underperformance anomaly.

The intan/at × lt/at core replicates "Identifiable Intangibles Tangible-Leverage Trap," and the added NEG(DELTA(intan/at)) leg is mechanically correlated with the intangible level through routine amortization, so it captures scale rather than impairment risk.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor" (same MA-R&D × 5-year-minimum-profitability template, merely swapping oancf/at for the already-tested ib+xrd addback from "R&D-Addback Liability Power"), so it is unlikely to deliver independent evidence.

The "distance above own five-year trough" recovery construct is a genuinely different state variable from the archived level/floor and delta formulations, though it is mechanically correlated with the current oancf level and reuses the che/lct leg already tested twice, so incremental information may be modest.

Economically identical to the archived "Goodwill Equity-Cushion Cash Burn" (goodwill load × weak equity × operating cash burn), differing only in decomposing the goodwill/(goodwill+ceq) ratio into a SUMRANK of its two components — a purely cosmetic reformulation.

Direct rediscovery of the archived "Capitalized Intangible Turnover Stress" with TS_RANK replaced by TREND on the same sale/at series and the identical NEG(oancf/lt) leg, which is an operator swap rather than a new mechanism.

A coherent and economically distinct test — using cash tax burden to separate value-creating acquisitions from impairment-prone goodwill, and notably inverting the archive's uniformly negative goodwill priors — though it is structurally the archived "Tax-Paying R&D Solvency" with the intangible leg swapped and is a very simple two-rank product.

This is the sign-flipped mirror of the archived "Knowledge Working-Capital Stability" (same MA R&D intensity × working-capital volatility), with only a bolted-on lct/lt current-liability-share leg, so it re-tests an already-measured relationship rather than a new hypothesis.

This is a MIN-mashup of the second legs of two already-evaluated signals ("R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover" and "Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor"), and because the two inputs are on incomparable scales — (revt−cogs)/lt is typically ~0.3–1.5 while TS_MIN(oancf/at) is ~0.0–0.1 — the MIN will almost always select the cash-flow floor, collapsing the signal into the archived Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor.

This is a straight SUMRANK blend of two already-tested archive signals ("R&D Maturity-Matched Financing" and "R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity") with no new economic content beyond averaging their second legs, i.e., a cosmetic combination rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

Although both legs share the lt denominator, txt/lt is mechanically an order of magnitude smaller than oancf/lt for most firms, so MIN() will be pinned to the tax term and the signal reduces to the already-evaluated "Tax-Paying R&D Solvency" rather than genuinely requiring dual confirmation.

Converting the archived level-based "R&D Cash Runway Commitment" into a five-year trend is a legitimate dynamics-versus-level distinction with a coherent forced-retrenchment mechanism and a sign that matches the expression's direction, though it remains a close relative of that prior signal and prior change-based R&D variants in the archive have generally been weak.

Since oancf is already net of cash taxes, subtracting txt/at converts (pi−oancf)/at into essentially standard total accruals, so the expression computes the Sloan accruals anomaly interacted with goodwill rather than the "tax validation" mechanism the hypothesis claims, and it barely differs from the archived "Goodwill Noncash-Earnings Quality Gap."

This is largely the sign-flipped counterpart of the archived "Purchased-Intangible Renewal Deficit" (NEG(xrd/at) becomes xrd/at on the same identifiable-intangibles base) with the second component swapped for che/act, which itself is the archived "R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity" leg, leaving little genuinely new to learn.

This is a near-rediscovery of the archive's "R&D Cash Runway Commitment" (identical xrd/(dlc+xrd) runway construction and identical first leg up to a 3-month MA), with the only change being +oancf in the numerator — a cosmetic ingredient tweak that also duplicates the (che+oancf) coverage idea already used in "Internal-Knowledge Solvency Mix."

It bolts a genuinely new component (a five-year gross-profit floor, distinct from the archive's oancf floor) onto the archive's best-performing but cross-sectionally weak "R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity," which is a defensible diagnosis-driven refinement, though the triple multiplicative rank risks compressing dispersion and inheriting most of the parent's alpha rather than adding new information.
